# Model Specification


The idea of this integrated MRP (MRP-INT) is to use the estimated inclusion probabilities as predictors in the regression models. 
## Inclusion probability following Valliant 2019
Let $S_i$ be the indicator whether the i is in PS or NPS by
\[
  S_i =
  \begin{cases}
    1, & \text{if unit $i$ is in the nonprobability sample},\\[3pt]
    0, & \text{if unit $i$ is in the probability sample}.
  \end{cases}
\]

Assign a weight of 1 to each NPS sample and fit a weighted logistic regression to predict the probability of being in the nonprobability sample. Valliant 2019 pointed that a weight adjustment is needed when the NPS size is not negligible to the population. Specifically, adjust the PS weights so that the sum of the NPS weights (i.e.,the NPS sample size) plus the adjusted PS weights equals the original total PS weight.

In more details, let $w_i$ denote the original weight of element $i$ in the
PS, and let
\[
\hat N = \sum_{i \in PS} w_i
\]
be the estimated population size from the PS sample, and let $n$
be the sample size of the NPS. The adjusted weight for
each PS unit is
\[
w_i^{\ast}
  = w_i \,\frac{\hat N - n}{\hat N}.
\]



Let $\mathbf{x}_i$ denote the covariate vector used in the weighted logistic regression model. Here both PS and NPS are used in this regression, and the likelihood is weighted by survey weight.

\begin{align}
  S_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i &\sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(\psi_i),\\
  \mathrm{logit}(\psi_i)
  &= \gamma_0 + \mathbf{x}_i^\top \boldsymbol{\gamma},
\end{align}

Then the inclusion probabilities are obtained by
\[
  \psi_i
  = \Pr(S_i = 1 \mid \mathbf{x}_i)
  = \mathrm{expit}\!\bigl(\gamma_0 + \mathbf{x}_i^\top \boldsymbol{\gamma}\bigr),
  \qquad \psi_i \in (0,1).
\]



We get two sets of estimated inclusion probabilities. The first is continuous $\psi_i$ to use as linear predictor in the outcome model. Then we construct A discrete inclusion categories $\Psi_g, g=1,\cdots G$ by rounding $\psi_i$ to one decimal place, such that observations within the same inclusion probabilities bin are assigned to the same group and share a common intercept. 



```{r, eval=F}
 ## 0) LOCK LEVELS FROM TRAINING --------------------------------------------
  nps_ca <- MR
  nps_ca$AGEP_binned  <- factor(nps_ca$AGEP_binned)
  nps_ca$SEX   <- factor(nps_ca$SEX)
  nps_ca$RAC1P <- factor(nps_ca$RAC1P)
  PUMA_lev     <- levels(factor(nps_ca$PUMA))  
  J            <- length(PUMA_lev) 
  
  ## 1) SELECTION MODEL --------------------------------------------
  # Build a clean selection dataset with shared covariates
  sel_MR <- nps_ca[, c("AGEP_binned", "SEX", "RAC1P", "PUMA")]
  sel_MR$S <- 1L
  sel_ps <- ps[, c("AGEP_binned", "SEX", "RAC1P", "PUMA", "weights")]
  sel_ps$S <- 0L
  
  # Align factor levels to training for selection model too
  align_levels <- function(df) {
    df$AGEP  <- factor(df$AGEP_binned,  levels = levels(nps_ca$AGEP_binned))
    df$SEX   <- factor(df$SEX,   levels = levels(nps_ca$SEX))
    df$RAC1P <- factor(df$RAC1P, levels = levels(nps_ca$RAC1P))
    df$PUMA  <- factor(df$PUMA,  levels = PUMA_lev)
    df
  }
  sel_MR <- align_levels(sel_MR)
  sel_ps <- align_levels(sel_ps)
  
  sel_dat <- rbind(
    cbind(sel_MR, weights = 1),
    sel_ps
  )
  
  if(adjust==TRUE){
    ## 1) Estimated population size from PS
    N_hat <- sum(sel_ps$weights)
    ## 2) Size of nonprobability sample
    n_np <- nrow(sel_MR)
    ## 3) Adjustment factor
    adj_factor <- (N_hat - n_np) / N_hat
    ## 4) Adjust PS weights
    sel_ps$weights <- sel_ps$weights * adj_factor
    sel_MR$weights=1
    sel_dat <- rbind(
      sel_MR[, c("AGEP_binned","SEX","RAC1P","PUMA","S","weights")],
      sel_ps[, c("AGEP_binned","SEX","RAC1P","PUMA","S","weights")]
    ) 
  }else{
    adj_factor=NULL
  }
  
  sel_fit <- stats::glm(
    S ~ AGEP_binned + SEX + RAC1P, 
    data = sel_dat,
    family = binomial(),
    weights = sel_dat$weights
  )
  
  #bin_val is 0.11, 0.12, etc, psi is the predicted psi, using bin_val represents the random-effect group which is used during poststratification.
  predict_psi <- function(df) {
    if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0) return(list(psi = numeric(0), psi_bin = integer(0)))
    df2 <- align_levels(df)
    p <- stats::predict(sel_fit, newdata = df2, type = "response")
    p <- pmin(pmax(p, psi_eps), 1 - psi_eps)#to avoid 0
    list(psi = as.numeric(p), bin_val = bin_fun(p))
  }
  
  psi_train <- predict_psi(nps_ca)
  psi_ps    <- predict_psi(ps)
  psi_pop   <- predict_psi(acs_pop)
  
  # Build a consistent bin map across ALL datasets
  all_bin_vals <- unique(c(psi_train$bin_val, psi_ps$bin_val, psi_pop$bin_val))
  all_bin_vals <- sort(unique(all_bin_vals))
  G <- length(all_bin_vals)
  
  
  bin_map <- setNames(seq_along(all_bin_vals), all_bin_vals)
  map_bins <- function(bin_val_vec) as.integer(bin_map[as.character(bin_val_vec)])

  
  psi_bin_train <- map_bins(psi_train$bin_val)
  psi_bin_ps    <- map_bins(psi_ps$bin_val)
  psi_bin_pop   <- map_bins(psi_pop$bin_val)

```

```{r, eval=F}
  bin_fun <- function(p) round(p, 1)  #round(p, 1)  may end up only has two groups if inclusion probs are small

  }
  
  psi_train <- predict_psi(nps_ca)

  # Build a consistent bin map across ALL datasets

  map_bins <- function(bin_val_vec) as.integer(bin_map[as.character(bin_val_vec)])
  
  psi_bin_train <- map_bins(psi_train$bin_val)
  psi_bin_ps    <- map_bins(psi_ps$bin_val)
  psi_bin_pop   <- map_bins(psi_pop$bin_val)
  G <- length(all_bin_vals)
```



## Multilevel regression


Let $Y_i$ be the binary outcome of insurance
coverage for unit $i$ in the nonprobability sample. Let $\mathbf{x}_i$ denote
the covariates, and let
$\psi_i$ and $\Psi_g$ be the continuous inclusion probability and its
discretized category as defined above. The MRP-INT outcome model is
\begin{align}
  Y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \psi_i, \Psi_i
  &\sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(p_i),\\
  \mathrm{logit}(p_i)
  &= \mathbf{x}_i^\top \boldsymbol{\beta} + \beta_\psi \,\mathrm{logit}(\psi_i) +\Psi_{g[i]}  + \alpha_{m[i]},\\
  \boldsymbol{\beta} &\sim \text{Normal}(0, \boldsymbol{\sigma_{\beta}}),\\
  \beta_{\psi} &\sim \text{Normal}(0, \sigma_{\psi}),\\
   \alpha_m &\sim \text{Normal}(0, \sigma_{m})\qquad m = 1,\cdots, M = 281, \\
\Psi_g \mid \sigma_\psi &\sim \text{Normal}(0,\sigma_\psi^2) \qquad g = 1,\dots,G,\\
  \sigma_\psi &\sim \mathrm{Exponential}(\lambda),\\
    \sigma_m &\sim \text{t}(\nu=3, s=2.5).
\end{align}
Here $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ are fixed-effect coefficients for the covariates
$\mathbf{x}_i$, $\beta_\psi$ is the coefficient on the continuous inclusion
term $\mathrm{logit}(\psi_i)$, and $\Psi_g$ is a random intercept
associated with the inclusion bin g. The inclusion bin random effects follow a Normal distribution with the standard deviation assigned a Exponential prio, where $\lambda$ is a rate parameter from data such that $\lambda = 1 / \widehat{\sigma}_Y$. Moderately informative priors are used for covariates, in which $\sigma_{\beta} = sd(Y)/sd(X)$ <span style="Si (2023) suggested 2.5*sd(Y)/sd(X), but it caused stan warning of -inf intercepts, so I used sd(Y)/sd(X).</i></span>. Finally, $\alpha_{m[i]}$ denotes denotes the random intercept for the m-th PUMA that unit i resides in, $\sigma_m$ follows half t distribution.


<span style="color: blue;"><i>J was used for PUMA and c was used for cells in the code. I changed the notation in the notes to use m for PUMA and j for cells, since Si (2023) uses j for cells and does not use areal level notation.</i></span>




```{r,eval=FALSE}

functions {
  real bern_ll_slice(array[] int y_slice, int start, int end,
                     matrix X,
                     array[] int psi_bin,
                     vector lp_psi,
                     vector beta,
                     real beta_psi,
                     vector zeta,
                     array[] int puma_id,
                     vector a_puma) {
    int M = end - start + 1;
    vector[M] alpha_slice =
        beta_psi * lp_psi[start:end]
      + zeta[psi_bin[start:end]]
      + a_puma[puma_id[start:end]];

    return bernoulli_logit_glm_lpmf(y_slice | X[start:end, ], alpha_slice, beta);
 
  }
}

data {
  // --- Training data 
  int<lower=1> n;
  int<lower=1> k;
  matrix[n, k] X;
  array[n] int<lower=0, upper=1> y;
  int<lower=1> J;
  array[n] int<lower=1, upper=J> puma_id;
  int<lower=1> G;    
  vector[n] lp_psi; 
  // number of psi bins
  array[n] int<lower=1, upper=G> psi_bin;   // bin index for each training unit
  // reduce_sum grainsize
  int<lower=1> grainsize;
  // ---prior
  vector[k] beta_scale;      // Vector of scales for beta
  real beta_psi_scale;       // Scale for beta_psi
  real sigma_psi_rate;       // Rate for sigma_psi
  
}


parameters {
  vector[k] beta;
  real beta_psi;                
real<lower=0, upper=5> sigma_psi;
  vector[G]     zeta_raw;
  real<lower=0> sigma_puma;
vector[J] z_puma;

}

transformed parameters {
  vector[G] zeta = sigma_psi * zeta_raw;    
  vector[J] a_puma = sigma_puma * z_puma;
}

model {
  beta      ~ normal(0, beta_scale);
  beta_psi  ~ normal(0, beta_psi_scale);
  sigma_psi ~ exponential(sigma_psi_rate);
  zeta_raw  ~ normal(0, 1);
  z_puma     ~ normal(0, 1);
  sigma_puma ~student_t(3,0,2.5);  
  target += reduce_sum(bern_ll_slice, y, grainsize,
                       X, psi_bin, lp_psi, beta, beta_psi, zeta,
                       puma_id, a_puma);
                       
}




```



## Poststratification 

For posterior samples, let
$\boldsymbol{\beta}^{(s)}$, $\beta_\psi^{(s)}$, $\Psi_g^{(s)}$, and $\alpha_m^{(s)}$
denote the s-th posterior draw of $\boldsymbol{\beta}$, $\beta_\psi$, $\Psi_g$,
and $\alpha_m$, for $s = 1,\dots,S$.

Following Si (2023), we assume the population counts are known and construct
poststratification cells using population data.  Let $j = 1,\dots,J$ index
population cells defined by combinations of covariates. For each cell $j$,
define:


- $x_j$ is the cell-level covariate vector.
- $\psi_j$ is the inclusion probability obtained by applying the selection model to the cell-level covariate vector.
- $\Psi_g = b(\psi_j)$ is the corresponding inclusion bin results.
- $m[j] \in \{1,\dots,M\}$ is the PUMA index associated with cell $j$.
- $w_j$ is the cell weight by summing each individual weight. Individual weight is 1 in population data.



For each posterior draw $s$, the cell-level linear predictor and probability
are
\begin{align}
  \eta_j^{(s)}
  &= \mathbf{x}_c^\top \boldsymbol{\beta}^{(s)} + \beta_\psi^{(s)} \,\mathrm{logit}(\psi_j)+ \Psi_{g[j]}^{(s)}+ \alpha_{m[j]}^{(s)},\\
 p_j^{(s)} &= \mathrm{expit }\!\bigl(\eta_j^{(s)}\bigr).
\end{align}


The PUMA-level estimate for area \( m \) is then
\[
\theta_{m}^{(s)} 
=
\frac{
\sum\limits_{j:\, m[j]=m} w_j \,  p_j^{(s)}
}{
\sum\limits_{j:\, m[j]=m} w_j
}.
\]

```{r,eval=FALSE}



# ---------- 1) individuals to cells ----------

collapse_to_cells_int <- function(df, train_ref, PUMA_lev,
                                  psi_vec,
                                  psi_bin_vec,
                                  design_formula = ~ 0 + AGEP_binned + SEX + RAC1P,
                                  weight_col = NULL,
                                  bin_map = bin_map,
                                  map_bins = function(bin_val_vec) as.integer(bin_map[as.character(bin_val_vec)])) {
  
  df <- .align_to_train(df, train_ref, PUMA_lev)
  
  w <- if (!is.null(weight_col) && weight_col %in% names(df)) df[[weight_col]] else 1
  w <- as.numeric(w); w[!is.finite(w) | w < 0] <- 0
  
  if (length(psi_vec) != nrow(df) || length(psi_bin_vec) != nrow(df)) {
    stop("psi_vec and psi_bin_vec must have length nrow(df)")
  }
  df$psi     <- as.numeric(psi_vec)
  df$psi_bin <- as.integer(psi_bin_vec)
  
  # critical: PUMA levels locked
  df$PUMA <- factor(df$PUMA, levels = PUMA_lev)
  
  cells <- df |>
    dplyr::mutate(W = w) |>
    dplyr::group_by(AGEP_binned, SEX, RAC1P, PUMA) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      w   = sum(W),
      psi = mean(psi),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  cells$PUMA <- factor(cells$PUMA, levels = PUMA_lev)
  
  # recompute bins from cell-mean psi (your logic)
  cells$psi_bin <- map_bins(bin_fun(cells$psi))
  
  Xp <- model.matrix(design_formula, data = cells)
  g  <- as.integer(cells$PUMA)
  if (anyNA(g)) stop("Some cells have PUMA not in PUMA_lev -> NA group id.")
  
  list(Xp = Xp, g = g, w = cells$w, psi = cells$psi, psi_bin = cells$psi_bin, cells = cells)
}

# ---------- 2) Extract CmdStanR draws ----------
get_params_int_draws <- function(fit) {
  beta_mat <- fit$draws("beta", format = "matrix")  # beta: S x K
  beta_psi_mat <- fit$draws("beta_psi", format = "matrix")  # beta_psi: S-length vector
  beta_psi_vec <- as.numeric(beta_psi_mat[, 1])
  zeta_mat <- fit$draws("zeta", format = "matrix")    # zeta: S x G   
  
  list(
    beta     = beta_mat,
    beta_psi = beta_psi_vec,
    zeta     = zeta_mat
  )
}

# ---------- 3) poststrat by cell ----------
poststrat_int_SxJ <- function(beta, beta_psi, zeta, a_puma,
                              Xp, g, psi, psi_bin, w = NULL, J = max(g)) {
  N <- nrow(Xp)
  S <- nrow(beta)
  
  if (is.null(w)) w <- rep(1, N) else w <- as.numeric(w)
  w[!is.finite(w) | w < 0] <- 0
  
  lp <- qlogis(pmin(pmax(psi, 1e-6), 1 - 1e-6))  # N
  
  # N x S components
  eta <- Xp %*% t(beta)                                  # fixed
  eta <- eta + tcrossprod(lp, beta_psi)                  # selection slope
  eta <- eta + t(zeta[, psi_bin, drop = FALSE])          # psi-bin 
  eta <- eta + t(a_puma[, g, drop = FALSE])              # PUMA
  
  p <- plogis(eta)  # N x S
  
  idx_by_j <- split(seq_len(N), factor(g, levels = seq_len(J)))
  mu <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = S, ncol = J)
  
  for (j in seq_len(J)) {
    idx <- idx_by_j[[j]]
    if (length(idx) == 0) next
    sw <- sum(w[idx])
    wj <- if (sw > 0) w[idx] / sw else rep(0, length(idx))
    mu[, j] <- as.numeric(crossprod(wj, p[idx, , drop = FALSE]))
  }
  mu
}



```

# Fit Model

```{r compile-model}
mod <- cmdstan_model(
  here("code/models", "mrp_int2.stan"),
  cpp_options = list(stan_threads = TRUE))
source(here("code/models","mrp_all.R"))
```

```{r fit-model, cache=TRUE}
# start_time <- Sys.time()
# fit <- [your fitting function]
# cat("Fitted in", round(Sys.time() - start_time, 2), "seconds\n")


start_time <- Sys.time()

 ps_df <- acs_pop[ps$idx, ] %>%
    mutate(weights = ps$weights)

# IMPORTANT: Bootstrap is essential for MRP-INT-R to achieve proper coverage.
# Without bootstrap (bootstrap=FALSE), MRP-INT-R only captures posterior uncertainty
# from the Bayesian model parameters, resulting in ~52% coverage instead of the
# expected ~95%. With bootstrap (bootstrap=TRUE, L=100), we properly capture both
# posterior uncertainty AND sampling uncertainty from the finite probability sample,
# achieving ~93% coverage.
tryCatch(
  {
  mrpint <- getMRP_INT(
      MR = nps_df,
      ps = ps_df,
      acs_pop = acs_pop,
      mod = mod,
      adjust=T,
      bootstrap=TRUE,  # Essential for proper uncertainty quantification
      L=100            # Number of bootstrap replicates (recommended: 100)
      )

    mrp_time <- Sys.time() - start_time
    cat("✅ getMRP_INT completed in", round(mrp_time, 2), attr(mrp_time, "units"), "\n")

    # Post Stratification results (MRP-R, MRP-P & MRP-R-bootstrap)
    rhat<-mrpint$rhat
    mrpra <- mrpint$puma_summary_mrpr
    mrppb <- mrpint$puma_summary_mrpp
    mrppc <- mrpint$puma_summary_mrpr_bootstrap
    cat("- MRP-INT-R results:", nrow(mrpra), "PUMAs\n")
    cat("- MRP-INT-P results:", nrow(mrppb), "PUMAs\n")
    cat("- MRP-INT-R-bootstrap results:", nrow(mrppc), "PUMAs\n")
    cat("- MRP-int-P results:", nrow(mrppb), "PUMAs\n")
  },
  error = function(e) {
    cat("❌ getMRP failed:", e$message, "\n")
  }
)


```

# Performance Comparison

## Calculate True Values and Direct Estimates

```{r true-values}
library(survey)

# Calculate true population values by PUMA (what we're trying to estimate)
response_var <- "PUBCOV"  # or whatever response variable you're using
alpha <- 0.05

true_values <- acs_pop %>%
  group_by(PUMA) %>%
  summarize(
    response_true = mean(.data[[response_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r direct-estimates}
# Add weights to PS sample (from test_sample.RData, ps contains weights)
ps_df <- ps_df %>%
  mutate(weights = ps$weights)

# Create survey design
samp.design <- svydesign(ids = ~1, weights = ~weights, data = ps_df)

# Calculate direct estimates by PUMA with standard errors
direst <- svyby(
  as.formula(paste0("~", response_var)),
  ~PUMA,
  samp.design,
  svymean,
  na.rm = TRUE,
  vartype = "se",
  keep.names = FALSE
) %>%
  arrange(PUMA) %>%
  transmute(
    PUMA,
    point_est = .data[[response_var]],
    lower_CI = point_est + qnorm(alpha / 2) * se,
    upper_CI = point_est + qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) * se,
    model = "direst"
  )
```

## Calculate Performance Metrics

```{r performance-metrics}
# Helper function for interval score (from main.R)
int_score <- function(alpha, y, lower, upper) {
  (upper - lower) +
    (2 / alpha) * (lower - y) * (y < lower) +
    (2 / alpha) * (y - upper) * (y > upper)
}

# Combine your model results with direct estimates
all_results <- bind_rows(direst, mrppb, mrppc)

# Calculate performance metrics for all models
performance_metrics <- true_values %>%
  left_join(all_results, by = "PUMA") %>%  # Replace 'direst' with 'all_results' when you have your model
  group_by(model) %>%
  summarize(
    MSE = mean((response_true - point_est)^2),
    MAB = mean(abs(response_true - point_est)),
    Coverage = mean(between(response_true, lower_CI, upper_CI)),
    `Int. Score` = mean(int_score(alpha, response_true, lower_CI, upper_CI)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

performance_metrics
```

## Visualize Estimates vs Truth

```{r visualize}
# Plot estimates vs truth for direct estimates (and your model)
ggplot(true_values %>% left_join(all_results, by = "PUMA"),
       aes(x = response_true, y = point_est)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower_CI, ymax = upper_CI), alpha = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~model)+
  labs(
    title = "Direct Estimates vs True PUMA Values",
    x = "True HICOV Rate",
    y = "Estimated HICOV Rate"
```
